unit: Reboiler B shell failure mechanism - vapor-pressure overpressure (primary, no liquid-full required)
limiting_value: Saturated Psat (95% propane per p.9): 18.75 bar abs = 257 psig (86% MAWP) at 130°F/54.44°C initial p.9; 21.07 bar abs = 291 psig (97% MAWP) at 140°F/60°C; MAWP 300 psig exceeded at ~61-62°C (~143-144°F); 24.92 bar abs = 347 psig (116% MAWP) at 155°F/68.33°C; 25.75 bar abs = 360 psig (120% MAWP) at 158°F/70°C; 34.13 bar abs = 480 psig (160% MAWP, 107% hydrotest) at 185°F/85°C p.9; 34.82 bar abs = 490 psig (163% MAWP, 109% hydrotest) at 187°F/86.11°C Task brief. MAWP 300 psig =21.70 bar abs, hydrotest 450 psig =32.04 bar abs ASSUMPTION pending verification (p.9 withheld).
evidence: bubble_pressure mixture 0.95/0.03/0.02: 54.44°C 18.75 bar, 60°C 21.07 bar, 68.33°C 24.92 bar, 70°C 25.75/360 psig, 85°C 34.13/480 psig, 86.11°C 34.82/490 psig, all errors []. Pure propane check 18.91 vs 18.75 bar at 54.44°C confirms <1% proxy error. Shell initially saturated at 130°F p.9 heated by tube-side quench 185-187°F p.9/Task brief after 08:33 opening p.11 Fig.6; ~3 min to explosion p.11. Shell 18.5ft x >5ft dia, 3020 x 3/4-in tubes, 24ft8in, 6-pass p.9 gives large area for rapid heat-up. Even with vapor space, MAWP exceeded after ~13°F rise.
modification: Recommended: A1 dedicated ASME VIII UG-125 shell PSV(s) set ≤300 psig discharging to flare/overhead, formally sized per API 520/521 for heat-input case (requires calculation + flare check, accumulation limited to ~110% MAWP per code) + A3 de-inventory/interlock. Alternative A2 remove/CSO gate valves p.10 Fig.4 restoring p.9 original shared column PSV design (availability penalty per p.9).

unit: Reboiler B hydraulic expansion (liquid-full) - bounding worst case if >78-91% fill at 130°F
limiting_value: blocked_in_pressure from 54.44°C/18.75 bar abs: critical fill 91.1% at 70°C, 79.6% at 85°C, 78.5% at 86.11°C; if above, hydraulic: 182 bar abs = 2620 psig (873% MAWP, 582% hydrotest) at 70°C/158°F with dP/dT 10.5 bar/K (β0.00599/K, κ0.000571/bar); 432 bar abs = 6260 psig (2087% MAWP) at 85°C/185°F with 13.5 bar/K (β0.00812, κ0.0006); 460 bar abs = 6660 psig (2220% MAWP) at 86.11°C/187°F with 13.9 bar/K (β0.00839, κ0.000602). Rigid-vessel screening - wall stretch lowers actual but still >> MAWP.
evidence: blocked_in_pressure T1 54.44 P1 18.75 to T2 70/85/86.11°C outputs above, regimes note decides vapor vs hydraulic. 16-month standby p.7/Task brief Feb 2012 implies cold condensation and liquid accumulation with vents/drains closed ASSUMPTION RFI-03/06. Small vapor pad compressed quickly then hydraulic. Explains catastrophic ductile rupture, pipe launch 30ft overhead p.11 Fig.8, >30,000 lbs released p.12, 2 fatalities p.12, 167 injuries p.12.
modification: Recommended: A1 thermal relief for liquid expansion per API 521 para 5.14 (small orifice, often ¾-in adequate, but requires sizing calc) + A3 keep standby empty/vented with N2 purge and DCS interlock blocking quench valves unless shell vent open/low pressure. Demonstrates why vessel burst violently even if not fully liquid - vapor case already sufficient.

unit: Overpressure protection defeated by 2001 design change (root cause) + quench fouling driver
limiting_value: Effective relief capacity 0% when shell/tube gate valves closed - p.10 Fig.4 isolating valves not in original design, installed 2001 p.9-10; original p.9 both reboilers continuously operating shared column overhead PSV with no trapped volume. Fouling p.8 oily tar from quench settler p.7-8 builds on 3020 tubes p.9, gradually reduced Reboiler A flow over past day Fig.5 p.11, impaired entire circulation p.11, prompting ad-hoc switch at 08:33 p.11 Fig.6. No dedicated shell relief - rupture at 480-490 psig proves no PSV lifted.
evidence: p.9 Williams installed shell+ tube side valves 2001 to allow one-reboiler operation while other isolated for cleaning when fouled; p.10 gate valves isolating reboilers from PSV at top of fractionator. No shell PSV mentioned - inference from failure. CSB Case Study 2013-03-I-LA MOC failure. DCS trend p.11 shows plant manager noted drop at morning meeting, supervisor volunteered (manager unavailable p.11), evaluated quench system p.8 practice, opened Reboiler B valves likely at 08:33 Fig.6. Shell 18.75 bar abs initial =86% MAWP already near limit.
modification: Recommended: B1 MOC per OSHA 1910.119(l) + PHA per 1910.119(e) including API 521 blocked-in/thermal scenarios for 2001 valves, PSSR 1910.119(m), fleet audit of exchangers with isolation valves; A1 add dedicated PSV per API 521/520 + P&ID update to CSO/blind for maintenance; B2 formal standby switching SOP with two-person verification, gradual pre-warm (open vapor first), manager approval, DCS permissive quench vs shell block position, fouling monitoring triggers vs hot-swap.

unit: PSM management system - human factors / 16-month standby equipment without procedure
limiting_value: Nonroutine reboiler switch performed alone without SOP, without operations manager p.11, on equipment offline 16 months p.7/Task brief with unknown trapped liquid pressure - organizational failure. Plant down 18 months to Jan 2015 p.12, 3.5-hr fire p.12.
evidence: p.11 group analyzed data after manager noted flow drop; supervisor relied on to troubleshoot; decided to switch reboilers and opened valves per Fig.6. No procedure described for bringing offline reboiler online, no vent/drain verification. 16-month dormancy with closed blocks p.9 implies no preservation/inspection. Quench 185°F p.9 vs 187°F Task brief ±2°F both exceed limits per recalibrated gauge comparison.
modification: Recommended: B1-B2 PSM upgrades - operating procedure 1910.119(f) for standby/temporarily isolated equipment, training, MOC, PHA, PSSR, audit; share lessons; implement DCS interlock + toolbox talk on blocked-in thermal expansion hazard per API 521; estimated one-time $100-300k for PHA/MOC overhaul vs 18-month outage loss.
